audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer is internally consistent as a favoured lane — diffRating 4/10, the green tone, 'Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10' — while full.diff alone says HARD, and the actual win rate is 46.67% over 450 games. The level chart gives Trundle 5 of 7 stages and Illaoi none.
audit.why: 450 games is the second-largest sample in the slice; 46.67% is a lane you lose slightly, not one you are favoured in. A chart on which the enemy never wins a single stage cannot describe a sub-50% matchup.
audit.corrected: diff HARD to EVEN, tone and diffRating to the even pairing at 6/10, and Illaoi given levels 4-5 and the two-item stage, which is exactly what whys[3] and whys[6] already describe.
sources: the entry's own whys[3] and whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike is written as a free win with no acknowledgement that Illaoi's own ultimate arrives on the same level and roughly the same cooldown.
audit.why: Subjugate is 120/100/80s and Leap of Faith is 120/95/70s. At level 6 they are both 120 seconds, so the level-6 window belongs to whoever still has R, not automatically to you.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now states both ultimates cost 120 seconds at rank 1 and to commit only when hers is spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is not only missing, it is inverted. The page tells you four separate times to Pillar near Illaoi — 'throw Pillar on herself', 'Pillar to break the tether', 'Pillar of Ice interrupts her E mid-cast', 'Pillar after if she tries to back away'. Prophet of an Elder God spawns tentacles on nearby impassable terrain, and Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain, so every one of those casts hands her a new tentacle anchor. Separately, Test of Spirit is described throughout as a tether that Pillar can break or interrupt — it is not a tether and there is nothing to break.
audit.why: Riot text: Prophet of an Elder God — 'Illaoi and the Vessels she creates spawn Tentacles on nearby impassible terrain.' Pillar of Ice — 'creates an ice pillar at target location, becoming impassable terrain.' Test of Spirit — 'rips the spirit from a foe's body... If killed, or if the target gets too far from the spirit, the target will become a Vessel.' The real counterplay is staying close to your own spirit and denying her the swings on it, not breaking a tether.
audit.corrected: Reversed the Pillar advice, and replaced the tether language with the Vessel condition: stay near your spirit, keep her off it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp is credited with an 'AS steal' in early and whys[0]; Harsh Lesson is never named anywhere in the content layer despite being her gap-closer.
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage only. Harsh Lesson is a 4-second leap to target that also swings every nearby tentacle at you and resets her auto — the 4s number is what makes disengaging from her field so hard.
audit.corrected: Replaced the AS-steal claims with the AD drain and named Harsh Lesson (W) with its 4s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing anywhere, despite the entry repeatedly saying she wins the attrition war.
audit.why: Prophet of an Elder God heals Illaoi whenever her tentacles damage a champion, so tentacle density converts directly into sustain. Grievous Wounds is what decides the extended trade the page keeps warning you about.
audit.corrected: Recorded here; not written into text because the itemization field is outside the fields I edited for this matchup.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit file's derived flags put 'grounding' and 'untargetable' on Leap of Faith and nothing in Riot's description supports either.
audit.why: Riot text for Leap of Faith: 'Illaoi smashes her idol into the ground, dealing physical damage to nearby enemies. A Tentacle spawns for each enemy champion hit.' No grounding, no untargetability. Per the tooltip-parsing caveat, the description wins.
audit.corrected: Nothing written; flagged so nobody builds advice on those flags.

edits.before: At Level 1 both of you are probing — take Q Chomp and short-trade her on the first wave; the AS steal already starts degrading her trade efficiency before she has tentacles up. If she walks forward to auto, that is your invitation: one Chomp, collect the heal from dying minions, disengage before tentacles can smack you. Do not stand still in range of a wall-spawned tentacle. At Level 2 grab W and hold Frozen Domain for the fight, not the approach — drop the ice zone after she commits, not before, so she cannot simply walk out of it. At Level 3 with Pillar available you have a real threat loop: bait her E by feigning an auto, and the moment she winds up the spirit rip, throw Pillar on herself to interrupt the cast or break the tether immediately. Keep these trades short; you do not want to sit inside a fully stacked tentacle ring trading sustain with her — she wins that war of attrition.
edits.after: At Level 1 both of you are probing — take Q Chomp and short-trade her on the first wave; the AD it saps already degrades her trade efficiency before she has tentacles up. If she walks forward to auto, that is your invitation: one Chomp, collect the heal from dying minions, disengage before tentacles can smack you. Do not stand still in range of a wall-spawned tentacle. At Level 2 grab W and hold Frozen Domain for the fight, not the approach — drop the ice after she commits, so she cannot walk out of it. At Level 3 Pillar arrives and the rule is counter-intuitive: Prophet of an Elder God spawns tentacles on nearby impassable terrain, and your Pillar is impassable terrain, so never place it beside her. Keep trades short; Harsh Lesson (W) is a 4-second leap, so she re-engages faster than you reset, and she wins the attrition war inside a stacked tentacle ring.

notes: The Pillar-of-Ice-spawns-tentacles interaction is the headline finding here and it reverses four separate lines of existing advice, so it deserves a second pair of eyes before applying. It follows directly from two Riot descriptions read together (Prophet of an Elder God spawns tentacles on nearby impassable terrain; Pillar of Ice becomes impassable terrain) rather than from any derived flag. Disk 46.67% / 450 games; packet says 51.27% / 197. Also worth noting: the kit file puts grounding and untargetable flags on Leap of Faith, and Riot's description supports neither — do not let any later pass build advice on them.
